title: A set of all effective gluing data for prescribed local module families
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and let module sheaves and their morphisms mean those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. All sets of points and sections are taken in a fixed Grothendieck universe, and the index sets below are in that universe. For each open $U\subseteq X$ fix a set $I_U$ and $\mathcal O_U$-modules $B_{U,t}$ for $t\in I_U$, where $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_X|_U$ and restriction to a smaller open is restriction of sections and module structures. Let $D$ consist of all tuples $d=(\mathcal U,(t_U)_{U\in\mathcal U},(\varphi_{UV})_{U,V\in\mathcal U})$, where $\mathcal U\subseteq\operatorname{Op}(X)$ covers $X$, $t_U\in I_U$, and $\varphi_{UV}:B_{U,t_U}|_{U\cap V}\to B_{V,t_V}|_{U\cap V}$ are module isomorphisms for every pair including $U=V$, satisfying $\varphi_{UW}=\varphi_{VW}\circ\varphi_{UV}$ after restriction to every triple overlap. Then $D$ is a set, and there is a family $(\Phi_d)_{d\in D}$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with isomorphisms $\theta^d_U:\Phi_d|_U\to B_{U,t_U}$ such that $\varphi_{UV}\circ\theta^d_U|_{U\cap V}=\theta^d_V|_{U\cap V}$ for every $d\in D$ and $U,V\in\mathcal U$.

source.place: Tag 01BC (lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules), proof: the collection of gluing data and coverings forms a set, and gluing supplies a module for each datum

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Op}(X)$. For an open $W$ and two fixed $\mathcal O_W$-modules $M,N$, a morphism is determined by its section maps [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)$ embeds into $\prod_{V\in\operatorname{Op}(W)}\operatorname{Map}(M(V),N(V))$: naturality, additivity and linearity merely cut out a subset. An isomorphism, together with its uniquely determined inverse, is a pair in $\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)\times\operatorname{Hom}(N,M)$ satisfying the two inverse equations. Hence every such Hom and isomorphism collection is a set in the fixed universe, by closure under function sets, indexed products and subsets.

source.place: Tag 01BC, lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules, proof: the collection of all glueing data forms a set; morphism encoding made explicit

proof.text: Since $X$ is a set, $S\subseteq\mathcal P(X)$ is a set. Encode arbitrary cover/label/transition candidates in the dependent sum $$E=\coprod_{\mathcal C\in\mathcal P(S)}\;\coprod_{t\in\prod_{U\in\mathcal C}I_U}\;\prod_{(U,V)\in\mathcal C^2}\operatorname{Iso}_{\mathcal O_{U\cap V}}(B_{U,t_U}|_{U\cap V},B_{V,t_V}|_{U\cap V}).$$ Every factor is a set by Step 1; the indices are sets, so $E$ is a set in the fixed universe. The conditions $\bigcup\mathcal C=X$ and the triple-overlap equations select a subset of $E$. This subset is precisely $D$, including all diagonal transition maps; therefore $D$ is a set.

source.place: Tag 01BC, lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules, proof: set of glueing data and set of coverings without repetitions

proof.text: Fix $d=(\mathcal U,t,\varphi)\in D$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] with index set $\mathcal U$, cover member $U$ at index $U$, and local module $B_{U,t_U}$. Its cover hypothesis is the cover condition defining $D$; its overlap isomorphisms and triple cocycle are exactly those of $d$, with the same order of composition and including equal indices. The all-equal cocycle is $\varphi_{UU}=\varphi_{UU}\circ\varphi_{UU}$, hence invertibility gives $\varphi_{UU}=\mathrm{id}$; thus the diagonal maps also meet the usual gluing convention. It yields an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\Phi$ and isomorphisms $\theta_U:\Phi|_U\to B_{U,t_U}$ satisfying $\varphi_{UV}\circ\theta_U|_{U\cap V}=\theta_V|_{U\cap V}$. No finite-type, separation, or finiteness hypothesis on the cover is required.

source.place: Tags 00AL (lemma-glue-sheaves) and 00AM (lemma-glue-sheaves-structures), via clause (2) of the cited module-gluing node

proof.text: Write $\mathbb U$ for the fixed universe and $S=\operatorname{Op}(X)$. In a larger ambient universe, $\mathbb U$ is a set, so section assignments $A:S\to\mathbb U$ form a set. For each $A$, addition, negation, zero and scalar multiplication are encoded by functions on the $A(V)$, and restrictions by functions $A(V)\to A(W)$ for every inclusion $W\subseteq V$. Their products are sets; the module, restriction and sheaf axioms cut out a subset. Thus these encodings form an ambient set of module sheaves with sections in $\mathbb U$. For each $d\in D$, encode the comparison isomorphisms and their inverses by section maps as in Step 1 and impose the comparison equations. The resulting witness set $W_d$ is nonempty by Step 3. The disjoint union of these witness sets over the set $D$ is a set in that ambient universe. Set-indexed choice therefore selects $(\Phi_d,(\theta^d_U)_U)\in W_d$ for all $d\in D$. Every selected sheaf still has sections in $\mathbb U$ and every comparison equation holds. For $D=\varnothing$ choose the empty family.
